title: Our Lady of Sorrows (15 September)
hookLine: the day after the cross, his mother

cards: Anyone who has sat beside a hospital bed knows the feeling of being unable to do anything. You can't fix it. You can't take the pain.
All you can do is not leave. Yesterday the Church lifted the cross high. Today, the very next day, it turns to the person standing at the foot of it.
Not the soldiers, not the crowd. His mother. The feast is Our Lady of Sorrows, and its word opens a medieval poem.

teach.b: John's Gospel gives the scene in one line, in the Douay-Rheims: "Now there stood by the cross of Jesus, his mother." She stood. The other Gospels say many watched from a distance.
John puts her close enough to hear him, and from the cross Jesus gives her to the beloved disciple, and the disciple to her.
In the 1200s someone wrote a Latin poem on that one verb: "Stabat Mater dolorosa, juxta crucem lacrimosa." The sorrowful mother stood, weeping, beside the cross.
It's often credited to the Franciscan poet Jacopone da Todi, though nobody can be sure. Today it may be sung at Mass as a sequence, and many churches sing it between the Stations of the Cross.
Composers from Palestrina to Pergolesi to Dvořák set it to music.

The feast also gathers seven sorrows that Catholic devotion counts in Mary's life: Simeon's warning in the Temple; the flight into Egypt; losing the twelve-year-old Jesus for three days; meeting him on the way to the cross; standing at the cross; receiving his body; and the burial.
Simeon's line is in Luke: "And thy own soul a sword shall pierce." In paintings, she's shown with seven swords in her heart.
What the feast honors isn't a mother who understood everything or could change anything.

teach.h: NOW THERE STOOD BY THE CROSS OF JESUS, HIS MOTHER.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of Our Lady of Sorrows on 15 September, the day after the Exaltation of the Cross; the Stabat Mater may be sung as an optional sequence, and some pray the chaplet of the Seven Sorrows.

games.q: you're Mary at Golgotha. the soldiers are there, and most of his friends have fled. what does John's Gospel say you do?
o: go home and wait for news.
games.why: she stood by the cross, close enough to hear him give her to the beloved disciple.

practice: Think of a mother who is grieving: a child lost, sick, far away or estranged, a child in prison; maybe someone you know, maybe a face from the news. Picture her standing where she has to stand, and don't try to fix anything.
If you pray, pray for her, or pray a Hail Mary for her; if you don't, simply stay with her in your mind.

wordCard.voice: Stabat Mater. Latin for the mother stood: the opening of the medieval poem about Mary at the cross, sung on Our Lady of Sorrows. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the sorrowful mother stood — the poem's first line.
